quality_check.description: A single vertical frame shows one closed dark violet hardback book on a pale layered paper ground with torn green and cream paper near the top. The cover visibly features a cracked alarm clock above a rumpled pillow, a partly drained tipped coffee cup near the bottom, and a cluster of dark crescent-shaped patches. Binding details, corner protectors, page edges, grain, shadows, and tactile cut-paper construction are visible.
violations: The book is substantially smaller than the requested 82–88% of canvas height, leaving broad top and bottom empty areas rather than narrow even margins.

The composition is not perfectly orthographic in presentation: visible book thickness, cast shadows, raised motifs, and dimensional corner pieces create a pronounced 3D papercraft/mockup effect despite the explicit no-3D requirement.
The alarm clock has a prominent top-center shape that reads like a capital 'T', conflicting with the prohibition on letters or readable marks.
The alarm clock face is cracked, but the requested partial obscuration of the fractured face by shadow is weak; most of the face remains clearly visible.
The requested muted navy component is limited; the cover is dominated by bruised violet and cool gray/lavender tones.
Heavy grain is present, but the requested soft vignette shading and compressed fatigued atmosphere are comparatively subtle.

The surrounding paper treatment broadly follows the reference's tactile torn-paper language, but it is cooler, cleaner, and more dimensional than the reference's warmer flat cut-paper illustration treatment.

prompt: Create exactly one 9:16 vertical first frame for an animated storybook transition. Camera is perfectly top-down/orthographic, never tilted or three-quarter: one CLOSED hardback book lies flat, centered and occupies about 82–88% of the canvas height with narrow even margins. The entire cover and page block are visible. The surrounding tabletop/paper/ground uses ONLY the supplied episode style reference's texture, palette and frame language; it must not borrow the book-cover subject matter. The cover itself is uniquely and richly crafted for this topic: What will happen if you sleep less than 5 hours a day. The authoritative COVER DESIGN BRIEF is: A closed illustrated book cover with a rumpled pillow centered beneath a cracked alarm clock, its fractured face partly obscured by shadow. Arrange a half-drained coffee cup near the lower edge, tipped slightly toward a scattered cluster of dark under-eye patches rendered as symbolic crescent shapes. Use muted navy, bruised violet, and sickly gray tones, with heavy grain and soft vignette shading to create a fatigued, compressed atmosphere. Render every named motif as visible cover craftsmanship — central emblem, border, binding, corners or page edges — rather than as tiny incidental decoration. Use ONLY motifs justified by that brief; do not substitute generic book imagery. No title, letters, numbers, readable marks, logos or real-person likeness. This is a closed cover only: no open pages, no two-page spread, no hands, no people, no UI, no photorealism and no 3D.
